### AB140 / 2025 Wisconsin Act 16

- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Robert Brooks; Sen. Dan Feyen and coauthors; R, with one D Senate coauthor
- **Status:** Enacted as 2025 Wisconsin Act 16; passed Assembly 2025-05-13 (91-6), Senate concurred 2025-06-18 (29-3), approved by Governor 2025-07-08, published 2025-07-09. No subsequent repeal found as of 2026-07-31.
- **Provisions:** Creates a conditional data center district exception to the TIF equalized-value limit for Port Washington Tax Incremental District Number 5 if created before January 1, 2028, and Beaver Dam Tax Incremental District Number 10.

### AB245 / SB244

- **Policy ID:** `wi-ab245-sb244`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Shannon Zimmerman; Sens. Romaine Quinn and Julian Bradley; R
- **Status:** AB245 introduced 2025-05-02 (Assembly Ways and Means), reached Joint Committee on Finance with passage-as-amended recommended 2025-11-07; SB244 introduced 2025-05-09 (Senate Agriculture and Revenue). Both failed to pass pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1 on 2026-03-23.
- **Provisions:** Introduced sales/use-tax proposal revised qualified-data-center certification, including a separate colocation/rental-services alternative and a cryptocurrency exclusion. Recommended AB245 AA1 replaces that alternative with standalone/networked server computing for an owner, operator or tenant, for themselves or others; changes the crypto exclusion from AND to OR; restricts qualified-investment spending to the business entity specified in section238.40(1)(b) or its affiliate; and adds crypto-based certification revocation. SB244 SA1 has matching amendment instructions. Committee recommendation does not establish enactment; both bills failed.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_support; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —

### AB840 / SB843

- **Policy ID:** `wi-ab840-sb843`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Shannon Zimmerman; Sen. Romaine Quinn and coauthors; R
- **Status:** AB840 introduced 2026-01-09, passed Assembly 2026-01-20 (53-44, Assembly Substitute Amendment 1 adopted); received by Senate, committee recommended concurrence 2026-03-13 (3-2), but failed to concur pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1 on 2026-03-23. Companion SB843 (introduced 2026-01-15, Senate Substitute Amendment 1 and 2 offered) likewise failed to pass pursuant to SJR 1 on 2026-03-23.
- **Provisions:** Introduced AB840/SB843 proposed infrastructure-cost protections, onsite siting of renewable facilities primarily serving a data center, closed-loop cooling, annual water reports, bonding and reclamation. AB840 adopted ASA1 targets defined large data centers, expands protection to all utility costs, allows cooling using no more water than a closed loop, and ties restoration after permit expiry to municipal requirements. Its renewable-siting, cooling and bonding provisions exempt centers already operating or under construction on the proposed effective date. Offered SB843 SSA2 additionally proposes local approval of certain wind/solar projects; it is not treated as adopted. These are failed-bill terms.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/amends/2025/REG/AB840-ASA1.pdf>)

### SB1061 / AB1099

- **Policy ID:** `wi-sb1061-ab1099`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sens. Chris Larson and Tim Carpenter; Reps. Darrin Madison, Francesca Hong, Supreme Moore Omokunde, Ryan Clancy, Angelina Cruz, and Angelito Tenorio; D
- **Status:** SB1061 (statewide data center moratorium, creating Wis. Stat. 134.44) introduced 2026-02-26, referred to Senate Utilities, Technology and Tourism; AB1099 introduced 2026-03-13, referred to Assembly Energy and Utilities. Neither bill advanced past committee; both failed to pass pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1 on 2026-03-23.
- **Provisions:** Failed proposed operation moratorium for facilities primarily storing, managing and processing digital data that satisfy any one of: at least5000 servers, at least10000 square feet, or at least100MW demand. Operation would depend on all14 safeguards being provided by law, as determined by the DATCP secretary: planning authority, utility/infrastructure cost protections, recovery funding, subsidy elimination, water/energy reporting, pollution safeguards,100% newly built directly accessible renewables, construction wage standards, restored PSC planning, NDA restrictions, local referendum approval and enforcement. The referendum condition is a proposed legal prerequisite, not an observed ballot contest.

### SB969 / AB1036

- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Andre Jacque; Rep. Clint Moses and coauthors; R, with later D coauthor additions
- **Status:** SB969 introduced 2026-02-06 (Senate Utilities, Technology and Tourism), committee recommended passage 2026-03-13 (4-1) but failed to pass pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1 on 2026-03-23; companion AB1036 introduced 2026-02-13 (Assembly Ways and Means) likewise failed on 2026-03-23.
- **Provisions:** Failed proposal barring political subdivisions and data centers or their agents from agreements, including NDAs, whose purpose or effect conceals development details or prevents public review. Introduced SB969/AB1036 operative texts match after documented normalization.
